name: Baked sweet potatoes with black beans, ajvar, and lime yogurt
time: About an hour, almost all of it in the oven
yield: Dinner tonight, two more potatoes for later
intro: Sweet potatoes baked until their sugars run and caramelize on the pan, split open and filled with warm black beans, smoky ajvar, cold lime yogurt, and feta.
needs: 4 sweet potatoes — two for tonight, two for later

steps.text: Heat the oven. Scrub the potatoes, prick each a few times, rub with oil and salt, and set them on a foil-lined sheet pan — the syrup that runs out will burn onto a bare one.
Bake without turning them, so the bottoms caramelize, until a knife slides in with no resistance and syrup beads out. Big potatoes can take an hour or more. Soft isn't done — keep going.
Stir the lime zest, half its juice, and a pinch of salt into the yogurt.
Warm the beans in a small pan with a spoonful of ajvar and a pinch of salt.
Split each potato lengthwise, push the ends toward the middle so it opens, and salt the inside.
Beans, then a spoonful of lime yogurt, then feta and more ajvar. The rest of the lime over the top.

how_it_works: A sweet potato baked long enough is rich and sweet on its own, so it wants smoke, salt, and acid against it: ajvar, feta, lime yogurt. The real technique is patience — soft isn't done; keep going until the syrup caramelizes on the pan.
swaps: Leftover sausage or pork instead of the beans.
Torn dates and feta for a sweet-and-salty version.
Kabocha wedges work the same way, in half the time.
leftovers: The extra potatoes keep four days. Reheat them whole, or cube them cold and crisp them in a skillet with an egg on top.

sources.note: 400°F, 40–50 minutes, and don't turn them so the bottom skin caramelizes
